I am 60 years old, and I have worked this land for 35 years. I know every mu of it like the back of my hand. My household has four people, so we have enough labor for the busy seasons, but I am not young anymore, and I cannot bend and lift the way I once did. My well gives me reliable water, and that is a blessing on the North China Plain.

This year, I will put **10 mu into my wheat-maize double cropping** because that is the backbone of my farm. It gives me grain for the household and steady income. The remaining **2 mu I will plant with cotton**. I have thought about dropping cotton—it breaks your back at harvest time and the price jumps around—but 2 mu is manageable, and the extra cash is useful.

For the **wheat**, I will sow my improved variety right after National Day in autumn. I will do rotary tillage before sowing to break up the soil. Over the growing season, I will irrigate four times: the overwintering water, then at jointing, heading, and grain filling. My well can handle it. I will spread fertilizer—about 18 kg of nitrogen, 8 kg of phosphorus, and 5 kg of potassium per mu. I have done this long enough to know what the soil needs. Two pesticide sprays should keep the weeds and insects down. If the frost holds off and the spring rain comes, I expect about 480 kg per mu.

For the **summer maize**, timing is everything. As soon as the wheat comes off in early June, I will plant hybrid maize directly into the stubble with no-tillage seeding. There is no time to plough between harvest and sowing, and I have learned that if I manage the residue and irrigate well, the yield is just as good. I will irrigate twice—three times only if July turns very dry. I will put down 16 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu, and spray twice for weeds and corn borers. I expect around 550 kg per mu.

For the **cotton** on my 2 mu, I will rotary till in late April and plant hybrid seed. Cotton is hungry for potassium, so I will give it 14 kg nitrogen, 7 kg phosphorus, and 8 kg potassium per mu. I will irrigate three times and spray four times because the bollworm never gives up. I expect about 230 kg of seed cotton per mu. My son will help with the picking in autumn.

I do not chase new fashions. I stick to what my 35 years have taught me. Weather is in heaven's hands, but good management is in mine.
